1.note: This marks a new part of the story.

1.q: commanded the building of a house for Yahweh’s name
1.note: The word “name” is a metonym for the person. Alternate translation: [commanded his people to build a house where Yahweh may live] or [commanded his people to build a house where they could worship Yahweh]

1.q: of a palace for his kingdom
1.note: Alternate translation: [of a royal palace for his kingdom] or [of a palace for himself]

2.q: seventy thousand men … eighty thousand men

2.note: It is understood that these are loads of materials for building Yahweh’s house. Alternate translation: [to carry loads of materials]

3.note: This is the name of a man.

4.q: I am about to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God
4.note: Here “name” represents the person. See how you translated a similar phrase in [2 Chronicles 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [I am about to build a house where Yahweh my God may live] or [I am about to build a house where people may worship Yahweh my God]
Solomon would command his people to build the house. Alternate translation: [I am about to command my people to build]
This is a reference to the 12 loaves of bread that were placed in front of the altar.
This was the time of a festival coinciding with the movement of the moon.
Here “This” refers back to all the ways the people will worship Yahweh at his temple. Alternate translation: [These are the things Yahweh has commanded Israel to do forever]

5.note: This is a reference to God being more important and more powerful than other gods, not to being larger than other gods.

6.q: who is able to build God a house, since the entire universe and even heaven itself cannot contain him? Who am I to build him a house, except to burn sacrifices before him?
6.note: Solomon uses a question to emphasize that no one is able or worthy to build a house for God. Alternate translation: [no one is able to build a house for God because not even the universe or heaven is big enough to contain him. I am not worthy to build a house for him, except as a place to offer sacrifices to him.]

8.note:
# Connecting Statement:

This continues Solomon’s message to Hiram, the king of Tyre.
These are different types of tress.

10.note: A cor is 220 liters. Twenty thousand cors equals 4,400 kiloliters.
A bath is 22 liters. Twenty thousand baths equals 440 kiloliters.

12.note: This can be restated to remove the abstract nouns “prudence” and “understanding.” Alternate translation: [who is very intelligent and understands many things]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **understanding**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “understands” or “wise.” Alternate translation: [who understand many things] or [who is very wise]
This is the name of a man.

14.q: He is skilled at work in gold … crimson wool
14.note: Translate many of these words as you did in 2 Chronicles 2:7.
Alternate translation: [high quality cloth] or [the best cloth]

14.q: He is the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan
14.note: Alternate translation: [His mother is from the tribe of Dan] or [His mother is a descendant of Dan]

15.note:
# Connecting Statement:

This continues the message from Hiram, king of Tyre, to Solomon.

15.q: of which my master has spoken, let him send these things to his servants
15.note: Hiram refers to Solomon as “my master” and to himself and his own people as “his servants.” This is a way of showing respect. Alternate translation: [of which you, my master, have spoken, please send these things to us, your servants]

16.q: you will carry it up to Jerusalem
16.note: Here “you” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [you will command your people to take the wood to Jerusalem]

17.note: The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon had his servants count]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [There were 153,600 foreigners] (See also: [Numbers](ta:translate-numbers))
“one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred”

18.note: It is understood that these are loads of materials for building Yahweh’s house. Alternate translation: [to carry loads of materials]
